name: Shades
title_tag: Custom Shades in Los Angeles | John Crawford Company
meta_description: Find custom shades in Los Angeles with John Crawford Company. Compare Hunter Douglas fabrics and controls, with measuring and installation from Woodland Hills.

sections.title: Custom Shades in Los Angeles, California
paragraphs: Tell us where the sunlight bothers you, how much privacy you need and what you like about the room. At John Crawford Company in Woodland Hills, you can see shade fabrics in person and work with us from selection through installation.

sections.title: Choose the room, choose the fabric
paragraphs: Start with how you use the room, when the sunlight is strongest and how much of the view you want to keep. A fabric that works well in the living room may let in too much light for a bedroom.

Look at the fabric with daylight behind it. You'll get a better sense of the color, how much light comes through and what you can see outside. Then compare the shade styles below for the shape and texture you like.

sections.title: Hunter Douglas shade collections
paragraphs: See how each style filters the light, folds or rolls up, and looks when it covers the window.

items.title: Roller and solar shades
items.text: Roller shades roll up at the top of the window. Compare solid fabrics for privacy with screen fabrics that let you see out during the day. Screen fabrics may leave a lit room visible from outside after dark.
collections: Designer Roller Shades: a single fabric panel that rolls up at the top
Designer Screen Shades: glare control with a view outside
Designer Banded Shades: alternating sheer and solid bands
Alustra® Woven Textures® Roller Shades: woven-fabric textures
Alustra® Architectural Roller Shades: fabric-covered battens that form a horizontal pattern

items.title: Cellular and honeycomb shades
items.text: Honeycomb-shaped fabric cells add insulation at the window. Light-filtering and room-darkening fabrics let you choose how much daylight comes into the room.
collections: Sonnette® Cellular Roller Shades: cellular construction with a roller-style design

items.title: Sheer shades
items.text: Fabric vanes let you adjust daylight, privacy and the view. Look at each collection open and closed to see the difference.

items.title: Roman shades
items.text: Fabric folds give Roman shades their shape. The fold style and lining affect the look, light control and how much of the window is covered when the shade is raised.

items.title: Woven wood shades
items.text: Natural woven materials bring texture to a room. The weave and lining affect how much light comes through and how much privacy you have.

items.title: Vertical shades and panels
items.text: For sliding doors and wide windows, compare how the panels open and where they stack. We can look at the space around the handles and the way you use the doorway.

sections.title: Daytime glare and nighttime privacy
paragraphs: We've used solar mesh shades in Valley storefronts to help manage glare while keeping a view outside. At home, a screen shade can help when afternoon sunlight falls across a television or the spot where you sit.

Daytime view and nighttime privacy are different needs. A lit room may be visible through a screen fabric after dark. If you need privacy then, we can look at a different fabric or an additional layer.
For a bedroom, we'll also look at room-darkening fabrics and the light that can enter around the edges. The fabric and the way the shade fits both matter.

sections.title: Measuring, installation and help afterward
paragraphs: Our service includes measuring and installation as well as shade selection. We check the mounting space and available controls, fit the shades and show you how to use them.
If a backorder changes the schedule, we'll keep you informed. If a question comes up after installation, you can contact us for help.

sections.title: Questions about custom shades

faqs.question: Can I motorize the shades I choose?
faqs.answer: Many collections offer motorized options. We can check what's available for the shade styles you're considering, your window sizes and the way you'd like to control them.

faqs.question: Can I coordinate shades in different rooms?
faqs.answer: Yes. We can compare fabrics and colors across the rooms you're working on. That may mean using different shade types where the light, privacy or door access calls for it.

faqs.question: What affects the price?
faqs.answer: Window size, fabric, product construction and controls all affect the cost. After discussing your budget and choices, we take professional measurements and prepare a quote.

sections.title: See the shade options in Woodland Hills
paragraphs: Schedule a showroom visit to compare fabrics, colors and finishes and talk through your rooms. If you're unsure where to start, tell us what you'd like to change about your current window coverings.

name: Blinds
title_tag: Custom Blinds in Los Angeles | John Crawford Company
meta_description: Find custom blinds in Los Angeles with John Crawford Company. Compare Hunter Douglas wood, faux wood, metal and vertical blinds, measured and installed for you.

sections.title: Custom Blinds in Los Angeles, California
paragraphs: Adjust daylight and privacy with a tilt of the slats. At John Crawford Company in Woodland Hills, you can compare wood, faux wood, metal and vertical blinds, with measuring and installation handled by our team.

sections.title: Start with how you use the window
paragraphs: You can tilt the slats to let in daylight, then raise the blind when you want more of the view. At a sliding door, vertical blinds draw to the side so you can walk through. Start with the way you use the opening, then choose the material.

Real wood brings grain and stained finishes. Faux wood is an option for rooms where moisture is a concern. Hold the finishes alongside the colors in your trim, floors and furniture to see what works together.

sections.title: Hunter Douglas blind collections
paragraphs: Compare the slat materials and finishes, then look at the vertical styles for wider openings.

items.title: Parkland® Wood Blinds
items.text: Real-wood slats in painted and stained finishes. Choose a wood tone that works with your trim, flooring and furniture.

items.title: EverWood® Faux Wood Blinds
items.text: A faux wood option designed to resist warping and fading. Consider it for bathrooms, sunrooms and other spaces where moisture or strong sunlight affects the material.

items.title: Custom Metal Blinds
items.text: Metal slats in a range of colors and sizes. Tilt them to adjust daylight or raise the blind to see out.

items.title: Aria™ Soft Blinds
items.text: Soft fabric vanes diffuse daylight and give horizontal blinds a fabric finish. An option when you want adjustable light control with a softer look.

items.title: Custom Vertical Blinds
items.text: Vertical vanes tilt for light control and draw to the side. We plan the opening direction around the way you use the window or sliding door.

items.title: Skyline® Panel-Track Blinds
items.text: Wide fabric panels run along a track and stack to the side when open. They give large windows and sliding doors a broad, paneled look.

items.title: Luminette® Sheer Panels
items.text: Sheer panels with adjustable vertical fabric vanes soften daylight across wide windows and doors. Tilt the vanes to change the view and privacy.

sections.title: The fit matters when you open the window
paragraphs: Handles, locks, trim and window depth all affect the installation. A blind needs room to tilt, lift or slide without getting in the way of the window or door.
Professional measuring helps confirm the fit. If you're considering blinds for several windows together, we can also talk through the layout and the way you'd like to operate them.

sections.title: One window is welcome
paragraphs: You don't need a whole-house project to call us. If you're replacing a blind in one room, we'll help you choose for that window and explain the next steps.
For a larger project, we can work through the rooms together and compare where the same material makes sense and where you may want something different.

sections.title: Questions about blinds

faqs.question: What's the difference between wood and faux wood blinds?
faqs.answer: Real wood gives you natural grain and stained finish choices. Faux wood offers a wood-style appearance with different material properties, including moisture resistance. We'll help you compare them for the actual room.

faqs.question: Can blinds make a bedroom completely dark?
faqs.answer: Closed slats reduce incoming light, but light can still pass through gaps and around the edges. If a darker bedroom is your main goal, we'll discuss suitable shade or drapery options as well.

faqs.question: Can you repair a blind I already own?
faqs.answer: We can review the product and available components. Send a photo and describe the problem so we can assess whether repair is possible. Parts availability and the condition of the blind matter, including for products from other brands.

sections.title: See custom blinds in Woodland Hills
paragraphs: Visit our Woodland Hills showroom to compare blind materials and finishes. We can talk through your rooms and answer questions about measuring and installation.

name: Shutters
title_tag: Plantation Shutters in Los Angeles | John Crawford Company
meta_description: Compare plantation shutters in Los Angeles with John Crawford Company. See Hunter Douglas wood, composite and vinyl options in our Woodland Hills showroom.

sections.title: Custom Interior Shutters in Los Angeles, California
paragraphs: Tilt the louvers for daylight and privacy, or open the panels for more of the view. See Hunter Douglas wood, composite and vinyl shutters at John Crawford Company in Woodland Hills, with measuring and installation by our team.

sections.title: Wood tones and painted finishes
paragraphs: A stained wood shutter can bring out the wood tones in your floor or furniture. For a painted look, compare the shutter finish with your window trim to see whether you want the colors to match.
For a bathroom or a room that gets strong sun, consider Palm Beach™ vinyl shutters, designed for moisture and sun exposure. The collections below let you compare them with wood and composite options.

items.title: Hunter Douglas Heritance® Wood Shutters
items.text: Real hardwood with painted and stained finishes, including wood tones that show the natural grain.

items.title: Hunter Douglas NewStyle® Composite Shutters
items.text: Composite shutters with a painted-wood look and a low-sheen finish.

items.title: Hunter Douglas Palm Beach™ Polysatin™ Vinyl Shutters
items.text: Vinyl shutters designed for strong sunlight and moisture. Consider them for bathrooms and sunny rooms where exposure matters to the material choice.

sections.title: Look at the panels as well as the louvers
paragraphs: Louver size changes the appearance of the shutter and the view when the louvers are open. Panel width and the number of panels affect how the shutters open into the room.
We can compare frame and panel options with you, looking at the window depth, handles and nearby furniture to see what suits the room.

sections.title: Privacy, daylight and bedroom light
paragraphs: Tilting the louvers lets you change the amount of daylight and the view into the room. Closing them gives more privacy, while opening the panels exposes more of the window.

Shutters can darken a room, but light can still enter between louvers and around the panels. If you prefer a darker bedroom, we can talk through what to expect from shutters and whether another treatment would help.

sections.title: From measuring to the finished installation
paragraphs: John's background in installation shapes how we look at a window. Along with the style you like, we consider the mounting space, fit and how the panels will open.
At installation, we check the fit and operation and show you how to use the shutters. Ask us about the panels, louvers or care instructions for the material you've chosen.

quote.text: Great service throughout entire process. From 1st consult to installation every step was performed professionally & with quality craftsmanship. Our shades & shutters are more beautiful than expected! …
quote.author: Mary Yingling, Google review

sections.title: Questions about interior shutters

faqs.question: Can shutters work on a door or an unusual window shape?
faqs.answer: Some collections offer door and specialty-shape configurations. We'll review the shape, dimensions, hardware and clearance to see which options are suitable.

faqs.question: Should I choose a larger louver?
faqs.answer: It depends on the look you prefer and the depth of the window. We'll show you the available sizes and consider the view, proportions and clearance together.

faqs.question: What affects the cost of custom shutters?
faqs.answer: The material, window size, panel arrangement, frame and finish all contribute. After professional measuring and product selection, we can prepare a quote for your windows.

sections.title: See the materials and finishes in person
paragraphs: Visit our Woodland Hills showroom to see shutter materials, finishes and louver sizes in person. Tell us which rooms you're working on and the look you have in mind.

name: Drapery
title_tag: Custom Drapery & Curtains in Los Angeles | John Crawford Company
meta_description: Plan custom drapery and curtains in Los Angeles with John Crawford Company. Explore fabrics, lining and hardware, with professional measuring and installation.

sections.title: Custom Drapery and Curtains in Los Angeles, California
paragraphs: Some rooms need curtains that close each evening; others need side panels to finish the window. Visit John Crawford Company in Woodland Hills to explore fabrics, lining and hardware. Our team also handles measuring and installation.

sections.title: Curtains and side panels
paragraphs: Curtains that open and close need room for the fabric to gather at the sides. Stationary panels stay in place to frame the window. We can compare the two with you and look at how much coverage you'd like.

Lining affects how much light comes through and how the drapery looks from outside. Length and fullness change the way the fabric hangs. We'll look at those details with you, along with colors and patterns that work with the room.

sections.title: Hunter Douglas drapery and related collections

items.title: Carole Fabrics® Custom Drapes
items.text: Carole Fabrics, a Hunter Douglas partner company, offers fabric choices for functioning drapery and stationary panels. We'll help compare color, pattern and texture, along with lining and heading styles.

items.title: Hunter Douglas Luminette® Sheer Panels
items.text: Sheer panels with adjustable vertical fabric vanes offer light control across wide windows and doors. This is another option to compare if you like a sheer appearance and want to adjust the view and privacy.

items.title: Hunter Douglas Provenance® Woven Wood Shades
items.text: The collection includes vertical woven options for a different texture at large openings. We'll review the available configurations, weave and privacy lining for the window or door you're working on.

sections.title: Give the hardware the same attention as the fabric
paragraphs: A rod or track needs to support the fabric and let it move the way you intend. We can talk through options for your window, including the span, mounting points and space for the fabric when open.
If you already have drapery and the rod or track is the problem, tell us what's happening. We can review the hardware and discuss whether repair or replacement is appropriate.

sections.title: Layer drapery with a shade or blind
paragraphs: You can use a shade or blind for everyday light control and add drapery for fabric, privacy or room darkening. We'll look at how the layers fit together so the rod, fabric and window treatment have room to operate.
If several windows share a room, it helps to consider how the treatments look together when open and closed. You can coordinate fabrics without putting the same treatment on every opening.

sections.title: Professional drapery measuring and installation
paragraphs: Professional measuring helps us work out the fabric, hardware and mounting details for your windows. Our team also installs the drapery, checks how it hangs and moves, and shows you how to use it.
One customer described the hardware side of a drapery project this way:

quote.text: Quick response by John to organize materials fabrication and excellent installation service … to replace damaged curtain rods in a 22 foot run of drapery. Highly recommended!
quote.author: Jan Edling, Google review

sections.title: Questions about custom drapery

faqs.question: Do I need drapes, curtains or side panels?
faqs.answer: The names overlap in everyday use. What matters is whether the fabric needs to open and close, provide privacy or finish the sides of the window. We'll start with those needs and show you suitable styles.

faqs.question: Can drapery help darken a bedroom?
faqs.answer: The fabric, lining and coverage around the opening all affect light control. We'll discuss how much darkness you need and review the arrangement, including light that may enter at the top, sides or bottom.

faqs.question: Can I add motorized control?
faqs.answer: Motorized drapery hardware is available for compatible arrangements. We'll review the fabric, hardware, opening and supported system before recommending an option.

sections.title: See drapery fabrics in Woodland Hills
paragraphs: Bring your ideas to our Woodland Hills showroom and see the fabrics in person. We can look at styles, lining and hardware together, and talk through any questions about measuring or installation.

name: Motorized Shades
title_tag: Motorized Shades in Los Angeles | John Crawford Company
meta_description: Explore motorized shades in Los Angeles with John Crawford Company. Get help with Hunter Douglas PowerView, compatible controls, installation and setup.

sections.title: Motorized Shades in Los Angeles, California
paragraphs: Adjust a tall window without reaching for it, or lower several shades together when the afternoon light changes. We help you choose compatible motorized shades, install them and set up the controls. Visit our Woodland Hills showroom or call to discuss your rooms.

sections.title: Choose shades and controls that suit your room
paragraphs: Some customers prefer a handheld remote. Others like the app or a control on the wall. We start with the way you want to use the shades, whether that's one window at a time or several together.
The fabric determines the light and privacy; the motor changes how you operate the shade. Start with the shade style you like, and we'll confirm which motors and controls are available for it.

sections.title: Hunter Douglas PowerView® Automation
paragraphs: PowerView® Automation lets you operate selected Hunter Douglas window treatments with a remote or the PowerView® App. In the app, you can set schedules for the times you want the shades to move.
We'll confirm whether you need a gateway for the controls and connections you want. At installation, we set up the system and show you how to use it.
sections.disclosure: The PowerView® App is required for programmed operation.

sections.title: Somfy motorization
paragraphs: We also install and set up Somfy motorization for compatible window treatments.

sections.title: Power options for motorized shades
paragraphs: Power choices depend on the product. Available options may include replaceable batteries, rechargeable power or a wired connection. For a tall window, the way you reach a battery or charger matters just as much as the control you choose.
If you're building or remodeling, we can talk through power options alongside the window design. We can also discuss the shade requirements with your electrician if electrical work is needed.

sections.title: A motorization job in Santa Rosa Valley
paragraphs: On a new-build project in Santa Rosa Valley, one of the connections for the hardwired shades wasn't working after the walls had been finished. We coordinated with an electrician to resolve the wiring issue, then completed the shade and app setup.

sections.title: Help after the shades are installed
paragraphs: We set up the controls and show you how they work at installation. You can also call us with questions afterward.
John has walked customers through recalibrating a shade in the app over the phone. When that solves the problem, there's no need for a service visit. Some problems need an in-person check.

quote.text: Wonderful and smooth experience. … The results are really just jaw dropping. Could not be better. Definitely spring for the Electric shades.
quote.author: Carol Larimer, Google review

sections.title: Questions about motorized window treatments

faqs.question: Can you motorize shades I already have?
faqs.answer: Sometimes. The product, age, condition and available components determine what's possible. Send us the brand and model if you know them, along with photos, so we can review the options.

faqs.question: Will it work with my existing smart-home system?
faqs.answer: Tell us which smart-home system you use. We'll check the shade motor, controls and any gateway or accessories needed to connect them.

faqs.question: Can I keep a remote as well as an app?
faqs.answer: Many systems support more than one control method. We'll confirm the combination available for your shades and show you how to use it.

sections.title: Talk with us about motorization
paragraphs: Tell us which windows you'd like to operate more easily and whether you're starting with new shades or reviewing an existing system. We'll help you work through the product, controls, installation and setup.
